# The Memory Chess

## A free chess memory game that asks you to study a position, rebuild it from memory, and review your score.

Screenshot of The Memory Chess website

The Memory Chess is a free chess training game designed for players who want to improve board vision, visualization, and spatial memory. Instead of focusing on openings or move calculation, it gives you a position to study briefly, clears the board, and asks you to reconstruct it from memory. You then receive an immediate score showing how accurately you remembered the position. [...] The game works for both beginners and experienced players because the difficulty can be adjusted to match your current recall. You can start with a small number of pieces and more study time, then gradually increase the challenge as your board memory improves. Short rounds also make it easy to fit repeated practice into a regular training routine.

### Key Features

#### Study and Rebuild Positions

The core exercise is simple: study a chess position, let the board clear, and recreate the position from memory.

#### Instant Memory Scoring

Each completed round gives you an immediate result showing how accurately you reconstructed the position.

#### Adjustable Difficulty

The game lets you control how challenging each memory exercise is.

#### Beginner-Friendly Training [...] Because the game is free and doesn't require an account, you can start practicing immediately. An optional leaderboard name lets you record your results publicly if you want to compare scores with other players.

### Train Your Chess Memory One Position at a Time

Study the position, rebuild the board, check your score, and repeat. The Memory Chess provides a simple way to turn visualization and spatial recall into a regular chess training exercise.

📈 Chess Improvement Guide

This page is part of the Chess Improvement Guide — A practical roadmap for getting better at chess — diagnose your level, build an effective training routine, and focus on the skills that matter most for your rating.

🧠 Chess Training Tools & Practice Guide [...] How does memory training reduce calculation mistakes?

Memory training reduces mistakes by stabilising the starting position so you do not misplace pieces during analysis. Many calculation errors come from incorrect recall rather than poor decision-making. Use the Chess Memory Trainer to reduce those hidden errors.

### Memory problems and frustration

 Why do I forget chess positions so quickly?

You forget chess positions quickly because they were not encoded with meaningful structure. Memory fails when attention is shallow or when the position is treated as random data. Use the Chess Memory Trainer to focus on patterns before rebuilding the board.

  Why do I keep making mistakes when rebuilding positions? [...] How does this chess memory trainer work?

This chess memory trainer shows a position, hides it, and then lets you rebuild the board square by square. That recall cycle exposes whether you remembered piece locations, colours, and relationships accurately. Use the Chess Memory Trainer rebuild board to discover which pieces disappear from your mental picture first.

  How do I start using the chess memory trainer?

You start by choosing a difficulty level, pressing Start Memory Test, studying the position, and rebuilding it after the board is hidden. The important training step is the recall phase, because retrieval strengthens memory more than rereading. Use the difficulty selector above to begin with a piece count you can rebuild calmly.
